nodes.name: Classify Expansion Families by Algebraic Field, Not Shape
nodes.statement: The research direction is to treat the pair of algebraic field and fiber group, rather than the polygon's shape, as the true classification object for expansion families.

shape.descriptor: reclassify geometric objects by their underlying algebra

sources.heading: 1.1 The Algebraic Field is the True Invariant
sources.quote: The proper classification object for the entire framework is not the polygon, nor the polytope, but the pair $(\mathbb{F}, G)$

nodes.name: Same Fields Recur Across 2D and 3D Constructions
nodes.statement: The pentagon, dodecahedron, icosahedron, cube, octahedron and tetrahedron all reduce to reconnection or distance-set conditions over a small set of recurring algebraic fields.

sources.heading: 1.1 The Algebraic Field is the True Invariant
sources.quote: the dodecahedron and icosahedron both over $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{5})$, the cube/octahedron over $\mathbb{Q}$, the tetrahedron over $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{2})$

nodes.name: Two Polygons Over the Same (Field, Group) Are Dimensionally Equivalent
nodes.statement: Two different polygons that share the same algebraic field and fiber group generate dimensionally equivalent expansion families.

sources.heading: 1.1 The Algebraic Field is the True Invariant

nodes.name: Golden Ratio Field Is the Universal Substrate for 5-Fold Symmetry
nodes.statement: The golden ratio is the unique quadratic irrational solving the 5-fold symmetry condition in any dimension, so any framework requiring 5-fold symmetry inherits the Q(sqrt(5)) arithmetic substrate.

nodes.name: Spectral Dimension ~1.1 Is Roughly Constant Across n=3..12
nodes.statement: Under the signed3 vortex rule, the KPM-measured spectral dimension is approximately 1.0 to 1.2 across polygons with n from 3 to 12, independent of n.

sources.heading: 1.3 The Spectral Dimension is Rule-Dominated, Geometry-Decorative
sources.quote: across $n = 3..12$, $d_{\text{spec}}^{\text{KPM}} \approx 1.0–1.2$ regardless of polygon

nodes.name: Vortex Rule Dominates Spectral Dimension, Polygon Is Decorative
nodes.statement: The vortex rule controls the spectral dimension of a multi-sheeted n-gon cover while the polygon geometry controls only the effective dimension.

nodes.statement: The four-level hierarchy of full reconnection, multi-sheeted full reconnection, edge-restricted reconnection, and non-reconnective tree is the natural classification of the entire framework, with edge restriction as the mechanism moving between levels.

sources.heading: 1.4 Pinwheels and the Design Space

nodes.statement: The number of distinct distances among n vertices of the pentagonal lattice is Theta(log n), in contrast to Theta(n / sqrt(log n)) for the integer lattice.

nodes.statement: It is unclear whether the observed constancy of the spectral dimension is an artifact of finite BFS depth or reflects an exhausted dimensional flow at that scale.

nodes.statement: The CA rule scales as B floor(n/3) over S, so the observed phase transition at n=5/6 is induced by rule scaling rather than by polygon geometry, and a fixed rule should track spectral universality.

nodes.statement: For each algebraic field admitting a finite orientation group, it is unknown what the minimal fiber group is that yields a locally finite, globally consistent expansion family.

nodes.statement: It is unknown how the Galois conjugation sending phi to psi on Q(sqrt(5)) lifts to an automorphism of the multi-sheeted graph pairing conjugate vertices on different sheets.

unresolved.description: Section 1.1's central claim is framed as an 'insight' asserted with confidence, but it is unproved and hedged elsewhere in the corpus; treated here as a fuzzy-layer conjecture rather than an accepted theorem.
The notes assert equivalence between multi-sheeted and cut-and-project constructions but never perform or name the morphism realizing it.
The universality of Q(sqrt(5)) is asserted as a number-theoretic fact ('5 is the smallest prime p ≡ 1 mod 4') without citation to a source document beyond this synthesis note.
